step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram features an ingestion flow from external Data Sources through ELB to a Kubernetes cluster running on EC2 instances. Consumers (agents/web users) directly query the Kubernetes cluster. Within the backend architecture, Kubernetes communicates bidirectionally with Amazon MQ for asynchronous messaging, connects via VPC Peering to MongoDB Atlas (with a return data path to Kubernetes), and interfaces directly with Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL) and Redis (ElastiCache) for authentication, metadata, and session caching.

edges.notes: Data sources send data streams to ELB
ELB fans out traffic into Kubernetes cluster
Agents/Underwriters connect to Kong API Gateway in K8S
Consumer web clients connect to Kong API Gateway in K8S

Amazon MQ delivers queued messages back to K8S microservices
VPC Peering connects into MongoDB Atlas
MongoDB Atlas returns processed data back to K8S
Keycloak and Kong API Gateway interact with Amazon RDS PostgreSQL
Microservices manage session state using Redis cache
